clone: git clone --no-local of HEAD 7b1cc73, then rsync of the 11:17 PST working tree (excluding .venv, .git, .env.local, vedit-sessions)

steps.result: Plan: 'uv tool install --force --reinstall --python 3.13 vedit[mcp,sam] @ <checkout>'. Skipped, as the README allows when uv and FFmpeg exist. The README says the script installs uv and FFmpeg; it does not say it also force-reinstalls a global briefcut uv tool.

steps.note: Warm uv cache on this Mac. A cold machine downloads CPython 3.13 and the wheels.

steps.meta_row: NO  meta                       no Meta API key. Create one at https://dev.meta.ai, then paste it in Studio Settings or set MODEL_API_KEY [required]
steps.note: The README says every [required] row must pass at this step, but the key is only added in the next step, so the required meta row always fails here. doctor also never reads .env.local, so rerunning it after pasting the key still fails unless the shell loads the file.

steps.step: cp .env.example .env.local (key left in the shell environment)
steps.studio_doctor_meta_row: NO  meta                       no Meta API key. Create one at https://dev.meta.ai, then paste it in Studio Settings or set MODEL_API_KEY [required]
steps.cause: scripts/studio.sh sources .env.local with set -a, so its empty MODEL_API_KEY= and VEDIT_META_MODE=standard overwrite the shell. .env.example says 'A variable already set in your shell wins over this file.' That holds for the Python loader, not for scripts/studio.sh.

steps.step: uv run vedit meta check (key in env)
steps.result: Meta credentials work. 9 models visible. Exit 0, no spend. Without the key in the env it exits 1; it does not read .env.local itself, so the README's set -a line is required.
Studio up; /api/capabilities meta.available=true, mode contributor. Port 8799 instead of 8765 to avoid other agents' Studios; --open skipped (headless).
